name: Identify all U.S. states, world capitals and flags
blurb: Three related memory projects that share a method. Once you have the map, capitals and flags attach to locations you already know.
gear: Quiz sites for states, capitals and flags
steps: Do the states first: 50 shapes and positions, learned by region — New England, the Midwest, the Mountain West and so on.
Attach capitals to states and countries you can already place. Location first, capital second, always.
Use mnemonics for the stubborn pairs: link the capital name to something about the place.
Learn flags in family groups: Nordic crosses, pan-African colours, pan-Arab colours, the Union Jack canton group.
Drill the confusable pairs deliberately — Chad and Romania, Indonesia and Monaco, Chile and Texas.
Test with mixed quizzes rather than one category at a time, which is how you find out what you actually know.
tips: Interleaving categories is harder and works better than blocking them.
The confusable flag pairs are worth their own dedicated deck.
proof: You score above 90% on mixed quizzes of states, capitals and flags in one session.
